title: Risk Molecule — Interactive Finding Relationship Visualization
goal: Show all findings from a run as an interactive force-directed molecule where node size and color represent severity, chain connections are visible as glowing lines, and clicking a node reveals full detail — making the relationships between findings immediately visible.
scope: Add a 'Molecule View' toggle to the Findings + Evidence screen (alongside the existing list view). In molecule view: (1) Each finding is an SVG circle node — size proportional to severity (critical=22px radius, high=17px, medium=13px), color matches severity (red/amber/yellow). (2) Findings that are part of a detected vulnerability chain (from backlog-43) are connected by animated dashed cyan lines. (3) Critical nodes have a pulsing sonar-ring animation. (4) Hover a node → tooltip shows title + target. (5) Click a node → the existing finding detail drawer slides in from the right (reusing backlog-59 drawer). (6) Nodes are positioned using a simple force-simulation (repulsion + chain attraction) without D3 dependency — pure JS requestAnimationFrame loop. (7) A legend shows node size/color meaning. (8) All data comes from the existing findings API — no new endpoints. The cinema_mockup.html Risk Molecule tab is the visual reference.
generation_reason: The cinema_mockup.html Risk Molecule concept shows findings as an interactive molecule that reveals chain relationships at a glance. No competitor shows finding relationships visually. This makes chain detections (from backlog-43) tangible and immediately understandable, and gives operators a completely different way to explore findings beyond the filter list.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: SVG visualization of existing findings data only. No D3 or external dependencies. No new backend endpoints. Molecule view is an optional toggle — list view remains the default.
